subject: Fencing validation: lab report, diagrams, and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <security@blueriverhealth.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <auditor@sig.org>
Date: 2026-11-26T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Fencing validation: lab plan and artifacts we'll hand off

Hi team,

Attached is the validation plan we ran in Redwood's dedicated-edge lab for BlueRiver's private deployment. Purpose: demonstrate tenant fencing under three injected failure modes (control-plane loss, cross-tenant egress attempt, and KV-cache leakage simulation) and produce evidence (logs, packet captures, diagrams) for SIG/SOC2 review.

Key asks today:
- Kimberly: confirm the diagram variant you want redlined (isolation-diagram-v2.png attached).
- Jasmine: can you add the batch of token-level latency traces into the runbook (validation-runbook-20261126.docx)?
- Sarah & Mark: we ran an initial lab; summary report attached (fence_lab_results_v1.pdf). Please review section 2 (failed scenarios) and tell us if you want deeper packet-level captures.

Short summary of outcomes (full details in PDF):
- Control-plane loss: automatic failover to regional control succeeded; KV cache warmed correctly on fallback shards; no cross-tenant cache reads observed.
- Simulated egress attempt (spoofed route): egress blocked at perimeter ACLs; generated IDS alert and connection reset; one test VM logged a misconfiguration (fixed during run).
- KV-cache leakage simulation: we induced keyspace overlap; our prefix isolation prevented reads across tenants but the test highlighted a monitoring gap in one metric (cache-hit ratio tagged by tenant) which Jasmine will add to the runbook.

I'll be streaming the raw artifacts to the Drive link below. If SIG wants an interactive walkthrough, Mark, we can schedule a 45-min call next week and run two of the scenarios live.

Attachments: fence_lab_results_v1.pdf (summary + raw), isolation-diagram-v2.png (annotated), validation-runbook-20261126.docx

Thanks,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <security@blueriverhealth.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <auditor@sig.org>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fencing validation: lab plan and artifacts we'll hand off

Thanks, Olga — good work getting this baseline completed quickly. A couple of notes after skimming the PDF:

1) Diagram markup: please add an inset showing the control-plane partitioning logic (how requests are pinned to regional management planes) and label the ACL entries that stopped the spoofed-route test. That will make it easier for auditors to map claims to controls.
2) Evidence chain: Mark, in the report we included checksums for the packet captures but not an MD5/SHA header in the PDF. Would you prefer hashes in a separate manifest or embedded?
3) Jasmine — target: add the tenant-tagged cache metrics and a short query snippet for how to re-create the leakage test. The runbook should include the exact traffic generator commands we used.

If SIG wants a live run, I recommend the Monday slot (11/29) 10:00–10:45 PT — we can reserve the dedicated rack and walk through the two failure modes.

- Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Reliability & Security Architecture
Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Liu <security@blueriverhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T08:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fencing validation: lab plan and artifacts we'll hand off

Appreciate the clear summary and the attachments — this is exactly what BlueRiver's security review team needed to start our internal risk analysis. A few follow-ups from our side:

- We will need the packet capture for the spoofed-route test with timestamps normalized to UTC; can you include an exported pcap with UTC timestamps?
- For the live walk on 11/29: we can take the 10:00 slot. Our security engineer (internal) will join; I'll send the sso account names and temporary lab access request to blue-river-labops@acme-labs.com.
- The one monitoring gap you noted: we consider that a moderate finding. Can you estimate the time to add tenant-tags on the cache metrics? Even a 2-week mitigation plan would help our compliance timeline.

Also CC'ing Mark (SIG) — Mark, if you want a pre-walk call to define acceptance criteria (e.g., what constitutes a passing result for the KV-cache leakage test), we're available Tuesday morning.

Thanks,
Sarah
BlueRiver Health — Security Reviews
From: Mark Chen <auditor@sig.org>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <security@blueriverhealth.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-29T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fencing validation: lab plan and artifacts we'll hand off

On Mon, Nov 29, 2026 at 13:12 PST, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Attached is the validation plan we ran in Redwood's dedicated-edge lab for BlueRiver's private deployment. Purpose: demonstrate tenant fencing under three injected failure modes...

Thanks for the artifacts. Quick notes from the SIG intake review:

- Passing criteria: we want to see (1) proof that a tenant-originated request cannot read another tenant's KV entries under normal and degraded control-plane conditions, (2) evidence that egress ACLs are primary enforcement and produce an observable alert on a failed attempt, and (3) a signed manifest of all artifacts.
- Please provide the manifest with SHA256 sums and the UTC-normalized pcap Sarah requested by EOD Wednesday (2026-12-02).
- If Redwood can run an additional KV-leakage test with tenant-tagged metrics enabled (even if synthetic), that will close the gap for the audit. A 2-week mitigation plan is acceptable as long as factual interim controls are documented (e.g., manual sweep, increased sampling).

Olga/Kimberly — once the manifest and pcap are uploaded, I'll re-open the SIG ticket and mark this as 'evidence pending verification'. We can then schedule a short verification call (30 minutes).

Regards,
Mark Chen
SIG Auditor
-- End of thread --
